title: Combat and Z-targeting
items: Hold Z to lock onto a target: you'll roll to dodge and strafe around it automatically.
A well-timed shield (hold B with a shield equipped) bounces back arrows and projectiles.
The spin attack (hold B, then release) deals extra damage but costs a bar of magic.
Jump while Z-targeting and attack in midair for a stronger downward strike.

title: Magic and bottles
items: The magic meter refills on its own over time; green potions top it off instantly.
A bottled fairy automatically revives you the moment you hit 0 hearts.
Lon Lon Milk heals in portions — sip it whenever, you don't have to drink the whole bottle at once.
You can empty an item bottle at any time to catch something else instead.

title: Bombs, Bombchus, and Deku Nuts
items: Deku Nuts stun almost anything nearby — great for breaking free from a crowd.
Bombchus hug walls and can be thrown into water — ideal for switches you can't reach directly.
A bomb tossed into an open mouth is usually the trick to a boss fight (Dodongo, Gohma…).
You can pick a lit bomb back up with Z + A if you change your mind.

title: Missable and time-limited items
items: Several trading-sequence steps spoil within minutes of real playtime — don't leave one half-finished.
The Piece of Heart from the white dog in Castle Town only appears at night.
Big Poes must be caught on horseback before they dissipate — always carry an empty bottle.
Treasure Chest Game chests reshuffle every attempt — there's no fixed 'correct' chest.

title: Getting around fast
items: Kaepora Gaebora (the owl) lets you skip long stretches if you accept his offer to fly you down.
Sheik's six warp songs are the fastest way to move around adult-era Hyrule.
The Scarecrow's Song works as a personal warp point once you've taught it.
Each dungeon map marks chests, the boss room, and any room with an unclaimed Skulltula.

title: Rupees and shops
items: Upgrade your wallet with Skulltulas (10 and 30) before you start hoarding rupees — overflow just gets wasted.
Every grotto's Business Scrub sells a unique item (arrow refills, Deku Nuts, extra hearts) cheap if you scare him first.
Sell spare gems and treasures at the Zora shop or the Bazaar if you need quick rupees for a one-off purchase.
The Shooting Gallery (Castle Town) gives a bigger Quiver if you beat a high enough score.

title: Gerudo Training Ground, room by room
items: Silver rupee rooms won't let you leave until you've grabbed every rupee in them — check corners and underwater before backing out to reset.
The Hover Boots turn the quicksand-floor room into a non-issue — just keep moving and don't stop on the sand.
One passage in the maze room is invisible without the Lens of Truth — sweep every dead-end wall with it before giving up.
The underwater rupee room wants the Zora Tunic and Iron Boots together, not just one or the other.
The Megaton Hammer knocks down the totem pole guarding the flame-locked chest in a single hit.
The final locked doors open in a fixed order — backtrack for any Small Key you skipped instead of bombing walls at random.
